bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42484477 (file): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 13 found by fuzz target magic_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42484477
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is exactly two bytes `ff ff`. In the second text-decoding pass inside `file_ascmagic()`, `looks_latin1()` accepts both bytes because the `text_chars` table classifies every `0xfX` byte, including `0xff`, as ISO-8859 text, so `ubuf` becomes `{0xff, 0xff}` and `ulen` becomes 2. `file_ascmagic_with_encoding()` then allocates `mlen = ulen * 6 = 12` bytes, encodes those two code points into only four logical UTF-8 bytes, and calls `file_softmagic()` on a `struct buffer` whose `flen` is just 4. On the witnessed `FILE_SEARCH` path, `mcopy()` aliases part of that 4-byte logical buffer as `ms->search.s`/`ms->search.s_len`, and `magiccheck()` calls `file_strncmp(m->value.s, ms->search.s + idx, slen, m->str_flags)` after checking only that `slen + idx <= ms->search.s_len`. Because the executed search rule carries whitespace-compaction flags, `file_strncmp()` takes the `strlen(s2)` arm at `softmagic.c:1917` instead of using the remaining bounded length. `strlen` therefore scans past the logical search window and eventually past the end of the 12-byte heap allocation, producing the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 13.

source.description: First project statement on the vulnerable path that materializes attacker-controlled bytes into the decoded text buffer later re-encoded and searched by soft magic. For the staged witness, both bytes are copied here into `ubuf` and `ulen` becomes 2.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly two bytes `ff ff`. `encoding.c`'s `text_chars` table marks every `0xfX` byte as `I` (`ISO-8859`), so `looks_latin1()` accepts both `0xff` bytes at lines 279-285 instead of rejecting the file as binary.

root_cause.code:
v = file_strncmp(m->value.s, ms->search.s + idx, slen,
    m->str_flags);
root_cause.description: The `FILE_SEARCH` caller knows the remaining bounded extent of the aliased search window but still calls `file_strncmp()` with only the pattern length `slen` and the flags. On whitespace-compacting rules this leaves the helper no bound for scanning `s2` itself.
root_cause.note: Immediately above this call, `magiccheck()` checks `if (slen + idx > ms->search.s_len) return 0;`, so the remaining extent `ms->search.s_len - idx` is known at this site. The staged patch adds a `maxlen` parameter and passes that remaining bound here.

sink.code: const unsigned char *eb = b + (ws ? strlen(s2) : len);
sink.description: ASan sink. `file_strncmp()` calls `strlen(s2)` on the interior search pointer instead of respecting the remaining logical bytes in `ms->search.s_len - idx`, so the read runs off the heap allocation created for the temporary UTF-8 buffer.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 13` at `file_strncmp /src/file/src/softmagic.c:1917:38`; the invalid address is the first byte past the 12-byte region allocated at `src/ascmagic.c:146`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The two attacker-controlled `0xff` bytes first become parser-owned decoded text here. Those copied `ubuf` elements are the direct input to the later UTF-8 scratch buffer that `FILE_SEARCH` aliases as `ms->search.s`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: Because `text_chars[0xff] == I`, `looks_latin1()` stores `ubuf[0] = 0xff` and `ubuf[1] = 0xff` for the exact witness `ff ff`, leaving `ulen = 2`.

parser_admitted.code:
if ((rv = file_softmagic(ms, &bb, NULL, NULL,
    TEXTTEST, text)) == 0)
parser_admitted.description: The converted UTF-8 buffer is admitted into the text softmagic engine here. The later `FILE_SEARCH` aliasing and `file_strncmp()` overflow happen inside this `TEXTTEST` scan.

evidence_limitations: The saved artifacts do not preserve which exact compiled `magic` database entry supplied the nonzero whitespace-compaction flags on the crashing `FILE_SEARCH` comparison.

The narrower source-grounded fact is sufficient for closure: the run reached `softmagic.c:1917`, and that line only evaluates `strlen(s2)` when `flags & (STRING_COMPACT_WHITESPACE | STRING_COMPACT_OPTIONAL_WHITESPACE)` is nonzero.

coarse_trace.summary: The two raw witness bytes `ff ff` are accepted as Latin-1 text and copied into the decoded `ubuf` that drives the later UTF-8 conversion.
A 12-byte UTF-8 scratch buffer is allocated from `ulen * 6`, but the converted text exposes only 4 logical bytes to `file_softmagic()`.
The selected `FILE_SEARCH` rule aliases an interior pointer and bounded remaining length into `ms->search` instead of building a NUL-terminated copy.
The `FILE_SEARCH` loop verifies only that the pattern fits inside `ms->search.s_len`, then calls `file_strncmp()` without supplying the remaining bounded extent.
Whitespace-compaction mode switches the helper to `strlen(s2)`, and that unbounded scan overruns the temporary UTF-8 heap buffer.

fine_trace.note: For each witness byte, `t = text_chars[buf[i]]` is `I` for `0xff`, so the Latin-1 decoder accepts both bytes and stores `ubuf[0] = ubuf[1] = 0xff`, leaving `ulen = 2`.

fine_trace.code:
mlen = ulen * 6;
if ((utf8_buf = CAST(unsigned char *, malloc(mlen))) == NULL) {
fine_trace.note: The converted-text path sizes its scratch buffer from `ulen`; with `ulen = 2`, `mlen` is 12. The saved ASan allocation stack points at this `malloc`, so the overflowed object is this heap buffer.

fine_trace.code: if ((utf8_end = encode_utf8(utf8_buf, mlen, ubuf, ulen)) == NULL)
fine_trace.note: Each `0xff` code point is encoded as two UTF-8 bytes, so the witness occupies only 4 logical bytes even though the allocation is 12 bytes. This helper does not append or guarantee a terminating NUL inside that logical extent.

fine_trace.code:
buffer_init(&bb, b->fd, &b->st, utf8_buf,
    CAST(size_t, utf8_end - utf8_buf));
fine_trace.note: The temporary `bb` buffer exposes only `utf8_end - utf8_buf = 4` logical bytes to the text softmagic engine. Downstream `nbytes`-based checks therefore reason about a 4-byte search region, not the full 12-byte allocation.

For the selected `FILE_SEARCH` rule, `mcopy()` does not duplicate bytes; it aliases an interior pointer into the 4-byte logical buffer and records the remaining logical extent in `ms->search.s_len`. This search window is length-bounded, not NUL-terminated.

fine_trace.var: slen, idx, ms->search.s_len, ms->search.s + idx, m->str_flags
fine_trace.note: The loop checks only that the current start position still has `slen` logical bytes available. The remaining extent `ms->search.s_len - idx` is known here, but the vulnerable call forwards only the interior pointer, the pattern length, and the flags, so `file_strncmp()` gets no upper bound for scanning `s2` itself.

The saved crash is at line 1917, which is only reachable when `ws != 0`; therefore the executed `FILE_SEARCH` rule carries whitespace-compaction flags and selects the whitespace-handling path in `file_strncmp()`.

fine_trace.code: const unsigned char *eb = b + (ws ? strlen(s2) : len);
fine_trace.note: With `ws != 0`, the helper computes `eb` by calling `strlen(s2)` on the interior search pointer instead of respecting the bounded remaining bytes behind `s2`. Because `s2` is not guaranteed to be NUL-terminated within the 4 logical bytes from step 4, `strlen` scans through the slack bytes of the 12-byte allocation from step 2 and then reads the first byte past `[0x602000000630,0x60200000063c)`, matching the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 13.

allocation_context.note: ASan reports that the invalid read is 0 bytes to the right of the 12-byte region allocated by `malloc(mlen)` here.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch extends `file_strncmp()` and `file_strncmp16()` with an explicit `maxlen`, replaces `strlen(s2)` with that bound, and changes the `FILE_SEARCH` caller to pass `ms->search.s_len - idx`. That is the exact missing obligation on the witnessed path. Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. The saved ASan stack is `strlen -> file_strncmp /src/file/src/softmagic.c:1917 -> magiccheck /src/file/src/softmagic.c:2154`, which is the exact project-side sink captured here.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The recorded stack covers `file_strncmp -> magiccheck -> match -> file_softmagic -> file_ascmagic_with_encoding -> file_ascmagic -> file_buffer -> magic_buffer`; the fine trace fills in the omitted but source-visible text-decoding, allocation, and `mcopy` aliasing steps between the PoC bytes and that stack.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. The two attacker-controlled `0xff` bytes are copied into `ubuf`, encoded into the heap `utf8_buf`, aliased as `ms->search.s`, and then passed as `s2` to the crashing `strlen` call.

poc.trigger: Use the exact two-byte witness `ff ff`. In the saved vulnerable run it is decoded as Latin-1 text, expanded into a 12-byte UTF-8 scratch allocation with only 4 logical bytes, and then reaches the `FILE_SEARCH` whitespace-compaction path until `strlen` overreads in `file_strncmp`.

format.name: 2-byte raw file input
format.contract: Use the exact 2-byte file `ff ff` and no other bytes. This GT is grounded only for that singular witness: both bytes must remain `0xff` so `looks_latin1()` accepts them as ISO-8859 text, `ulen` stays 2, `file_ascmagic_with_encoding()` allocates `ulen * 6 = 12` bytes, and the later text `FILE_SEARCH` path reaches the unbounded `strlen(s2)` call. Stage 02 does not generalize beyond this exact two-byte sample.
